title: Working with George Schilling's band after returning from the north
summary: Back in New Orleans he worked nightly with Schilling, whose band played arranged jazz with a good lineup and a rhythm section of Johnny Frisco and Eddie Hyman.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You were saying you worked with Shilling yourself.

After I came back here, I was up north, you see. Yeah. I came back here. I stood here about two years, you see. That was Spartan with Shilling. You know? Yeah. Spartan. Spartan. Shilling had the town sold out. I'll tell you how he had the town sold out with music. See, my father had a business. I was always learning how to cut meat from a child to a child. And me being the only son, my daddy always wanted me by him. You know what I mean? I wasn't no papa's boy, but still no. He was the papa and I was the boss. Everything I said, you know, he wanted me by him. So I came down there and I was with George. And I worked with my daddy in the market. So I started Spartan with George. And he had us going every night. See, at that time, I didn't need no money. I didn't need no money. I had everything I wanted. But I just loved to play music. See? So I got tired and then I wanted to take a trip again. See? Young father. You understand? But like I worked with George Shields. He had us going every night a week. I hear Bracay was with us, too. Oh, yeah. Shield, Bracay. And after I shield left, you know, I kind of got disgusted. You know what I mean? I left down a few hours. I don't know. I shield worked with us.
How many cornets did you use with Shields? Two.

We had the first one, he's dead, Harry Shannon. Then I had, we had Henrikh Konek with us. And we had Dan Tyler playing sax. We had a wonderful little jazz band. And at that time we were, we were, you see, in them days, most of these bands would run around playing with nothing but chords. You know what I mean? But they'd stick on the chords and funny facts. But George, we played music. Then we used to mix it in. You know what I mean? And we harmonized, you see? Then they had that wind jam, you know what I mean? All of them blasting music, you see? But George and I, we started playing jazz. But like, just like Paul White, we came along and made this symphonic, you know, with jazz. You understand? And that's why we were going big over there. We were going big because George would take a job. And someone would come along and they would sing, they would snap, they would sing. Well, we had the music, we played. But these other bands, you'd have, maybe about two men would lead. And the other's couldn't. But remember, you couldn't go play that stuff, you understand, son? You had, you know? But George had all good men. Everyone read but him. He's man-made of them. He said it. He always said it. He's man-made.
Who did he have in the rhythm section then?
In the rhythm section, Johnny Frisco and Eddie Hyman, who's a bass player. I know him.
